text: Mr. Alvarez, a retired teacher, spilled red wine on his best white shirt, and dinner with old friends was only two hours away. It was an urgent job. He grabbed his phone and typed fast: how long is the quik wash, i need the shirt clean. The assistant understood that he wanted to know how long the quick cycle took on his washing machine. It said the quick wash takes thirty-five minutes. Then Mr. Alvarez typed, start it and tell me when it's done. The assistant started the quick wash and set a timer to track the time. Every hour of the evening was planned, so he was glad to have a clear answer. When the machine finished, the phone chimed, and the assistant said the shirt was clean and could go in the dryer.

Rosa runs a small gift shop near the harbor. One afternoon a tourist wanted to pay for a scarf with a coin from home and a few paper notes, and Rosa was not sure what they were worth. She said to her phone, how much is twenty-five euros in dollars today? The assistant understood that she wanted the exchange rate, worked out the amount, and told her the answer in dollars. Rosa also asked it to alert her when the rate got better, because the money kept changing in constant small steps. The assistant said it would send her a message when the rate moved by a good amount. Rosa thanked the tourist, put the money in the till, and wrapped the scarf with a smile.

A playlist is a list of songs that play one after another. People use playlists when they cook, drive, clean or study. Most people change just a few things: the volume, which song plays next, and the order of the songs. To make the music louder they say, turn it up a little, or, I wish it were quieter. To skip a song they say, next one, or, skip this. Some people say something silly like, hit the brake on this song, when they only mean pause it. A good assistant knows that pause, stop and hold on mean nearly the same thing. If you want to hear a song again, you can say, play that one again, or, go back.

An air purifier cleans the air in a room by pulling it through a filter. People use one when the air feels stuffy, when there is smoke outside, or when someone at home is sick. What do people change? Mostly the fan speed, the timer and the mode. They say, make it stronger, run it quietly tonight, or, turn it off in an hour. A humidifier is a little like it: it adds water to dry air, and people ask for more or less. Cooking a big pot of soup can fill a kitchen with steam, so some people open a window or switch on the fan over the stove. If the room still feels heavy, they repeat the request: turn the purifier up, please.

The sea changes through the day. At high tide the water comes far up the sand, and at low tide it goes back out. Swimming can be difficult when the tide pulls hard, so many people check the tide times before they go. Sun cream protects your skin, and most people put it on again every two hours. People also like to know how warm the water is. They ask things like, what time is high tide, is the water cold today, or, how strong is the sun right now? After a swim, many people drink hot tea from a flask and dry off in the sun. If you want the numbers for another place, you can say, check the next beach along instead.

name: line_watcher
does: Tells how long the line is at a post office or bank branch right now.
inputs: the branch or its street, and the time the person plans to go if they have one
people say:
- how busy is the post office right now
- is there a long wait at the bank on Main Street
- give me a signal when the line gets short
- should I go out on this icy morning or will the bank be quiet later
- does the branch welcome walk-ins at lunchtime or will I be stuck waiting

Subtitles are the words at the bottom of the screen that show what people are saying. They help when a room is noisy, when a baby is asleep, or when someone cannot hear well. A family on a camping trip may watch a little show on a tablet with the sound off, and subtitles let them follow the story. People change a few things about them: they turn them on or off, make the letters bigger, or pick another language. They say, put the words on, the text is too small, or, switch the subtitles to Spanish. Sometimes people say, what does that mean, when they cannot read a word fast enough, and ask to go back ten seconds to read it again.

Tom was nine, and he wanted to cook pancakes for his sister while she worked on a puzzle at the table. The recipe made twelve pancakes, which was too many. Tom said to the kitchen speaker, make this recipe for four people. No wait, for three, it's just me, Dad and Anna. The assistant understood that Tom had changed his mind and made the recipe again for three. It said the small batch needed one cup of flour, one egg and one cup of milk, and it read the amounts slowly. Tom measured each thing and said next after every step. The assistant waited and read the next line when he asked. Soon the kitchen smelled warm and sweet, and Anna put her puzzle away.

name: arrival_tracker
does: Shows when a food order will arrive and how far away the driver is.
inputs: which order, if the person has more than one open
people say:
- where is my pizza
- how long until my dozen dumplings get here
- is the driver close yet
- the map looks weird, did the driver get lost
- does the app lie, it said ten minutes an hour ago

Most people have more than one account at a bank, for example one for daily spending and one for savings. The balance is the amount of money in an account. A transfer moves money from one of your accounts to another. People do this when a spending account is nearly empty or when they want to save more. On many apps you can even drag the money from one account to the other with a finger. They say, move fifty dollars to savings, put some money into my checking account, or, send what's left to savings. A sharp eye on the balance helps, so people often ask, how much do I have, or, what's left in checking? If a card is lost, they say, freeze my card.

Lena, a student, was packing for a weekend hike in the hills, and her train left soon, so it was urgent. She said to her phone, what will the weather be like on Saturday, and add a rain jacket to my packing list. The assistant understood two things in one sentence: she wanted the forecast for the hills, and she wanted one more item on her list. It said Saturday would be cool with light rain, and it added the rain jacket below the tent and the water bottle. Lena knew that high up in the hills she would breathe harder, so she packed extra snacks too. She had paid for the train with her student account, and the ticket was already on her phone. She locked the door and ran to the station.

Person: Good morning. I am a retired teacher, and I am moving to a smaller flat next month, so I would be very grateful if you could set a reminder for me.
Assistant: Of course. What should the reminder say?
Person: Please remind me to call the electric company, so the power is on in the new flat on the first day.
Assistant: Which day should I remind you?
Person: The third of the month, in the morning. I find that I forget things when I am busy with boxes.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you on the third at nine in the morning. Should I also remind you about the water bill?
Person: Not yet. My budget is low this month, so I will wait.
Assistant: All right. Good luck with the move.

Person: Heat pool.
Assistant: Which pool should I heat, the front one or the back one?
Person: Front. My aunt is visiting and she hates cold water.
Assistant: What temperature would you like?
Person: Eighty degrees. Don't let it drop below that.
Assistant: Okay. I will heat the front pool to eighty and keep it there. Do you want it ready by noon?
Person: Yes, please.

Marco, a cook, was writing the menu card for his little restaurant. His hands were greasy from the grill, so he talked to his phone instead of typing. Spell bruschetta, he said. The assistant spelled it letter by letter: b, r, u, s, c, h, e, t, t, a. Marco wrote it down and smiled. His next line read roasted garlic bulb on delicious grilled bread, and he wanted to know if it was too long. Word count, he said. The assistant understood that he wanted the number of words in the draft so far, and it told him there were forty-one. Marco cut a few words, asked again, and the assistant said thirty-six. The menu card was ready to print.

Brightness is how strong the light from a phone screen is. Outside in the sun, people turn it up so they can see the screen. At night they turn it down so it does not hurt their eyes. Battery saver makes the charge last longer, and do not disturb stops calls and sounds while you sleep. People say, make the screen brighter, dim it a little, or, silence my phone until morning. When a new phone comes, you peel the thin plastic sheet off the screen before you start. Joggers sometimes clip a small phone to a jacket collar, and they ask for a quiet screen so the light does not bounce around. Storage is the space for photos and apps, and people ask, how much room do I have left?

name: wash_setting_picker
does: Chooses the right washing machine setting for a kind of clothes and starts it.
inputs: the kind of clothes or fabric, and how dirty they are
people say:
- wash my wool sweaters gently
- I don't understand which setting is for towels, just pick one
- the bedsheets are really dirty, give them a strong wash
- run something quiet, the baby is asleep
- the delicates bag is in the drum, start it

Person: How many days until my tomatoes are ready?
Assistant: I can count that for you. What day did you plant them?
Person: The third of May. The seed packet said seventy days.
Assistant: Seventy days after the third of May is the twelfth of July.
Person: Wonderful. I often forget dates, so can you remind me?
Assistant: Yes. Should I remind you on the day, or a few days before?
Person: A week before. Then I can wave over the fence and offer some to my neighbors.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you on the fifth of July.

When you buy something online, the store usually sends you a tracking number. You can use it to see where your package is, and many people simply ask, where is my order, or, when will it come? If a delivery is late, people say, explain why it is delayed, or, can you tell me the new date? Sometimes the thing you get is not what you wanted, such as a lamp with less brightness than you hoped, and then you ask for a refund. Fresh food, like a creamy cheese, has to arrive cold, so people check the time and ask for a window. A refund can take a few days to come back to your card.

Jonas, a student, was planning a birthday party for his roommate, and he was bad at keeping lists in his head. He asked his phone, how many people did I invite? The assistant counted the guest list and said twenty-five. Jonas then asked how to spell congratulations for the banner he was painting, and the assistant spelled it slowly, letter by letter. He also said, play something fun, and the assistant started a party playlist at a low volume. Later, when the big game came on during the party, he asked, what's the score? The assistant understood he meant the soccer match and read the score aloud. Everyone cheered, and the night went well.

Person: I want to post a photo of my dinner, but I don't want everyone to see it.
Assistant: Who should see it? Everyone you follow, or just a small group?
Person: Just my close friends.
Assistant: Okay. Which photo should I use?
Person: The one of the pan of pasta. It looks delicious.
Assistant: I found it. Do you want to add a caption?
Person: Yes, write Sunday dinner. No hashtags, please.
Assistant: Posted to close friends with the caption Sunday dinner and no hashtags.

A bank balance is the amount of money you have in an account right now. Checking it helps you decide what you can spend, whether it is a night at the theater or a week of groceries. People check it often and ask, what's my balance, or, how much is left? A transfer moves money between your own accounts, and on many apps you can drag the money from one account to another with a finger. When a fee appears that nobody expected, people get angry and ask, why was I charged? They also ask for more or less money to be moved, using words like, put in a bit more, or, take out twenty.

Painting is a hobby where an artist puts color on paper or cloth with brushes. People paint to relax, to make a gift, or just to see what happens. They change things as they go: the color, the size of the brush, how thick the paint is, and how long to wait. They say, make it a little darker, use a bigger brush, or, I need a pair of clean brushes. Many hobbies work this way, from knitting to building models. When the paint is wet, people ask an assistant to set a timer, and they say, tell me when it's ready. Then they can come back and add the next layer.

Grandpa Joe sat at his computer with a cup of bitter coffee. He wanted to read an article about gardens, but the screen was dim and gray. He sighed and said, I can't see a thing in here. The assistant understood that he meant the screen was too dark, and it made the screen brighter. Joe squinted and muttered, these letters are so small, they look like a slice of a stamp. The assistant understood that he wanted bigger text and made the words larger. Now the article was easy to read. Joe said thank you, took another sip of his coffee, and read about tomatoes all morning.

Ordering food to your door is simple. You pick a restaurant, choose your dishes, and pay in the app. The app shows a delivery time, and a driver brings the food. A doctor on a night shift might order dinner this way, since there is no time to cook. The app may warn you when a place is very busy, and then the time gets longer. People change a few things: the address, the dishes, and the tip. They add special instructions too, like no onions or leave it at the door. They say, make that two burgers, add a bigger tip, or, change the address to my office.

They want to know how many days are left until a date.
how many dasy until my trip
How long until Friday?
What's the countdown to Christmas?
How many sleeps until the holiday?
I'd cry if I forgot our gold anniversary, so how far away is it?
I left my glasses at the shop, so please count the days until they are ready on the twentieth.
Would you be so kind as to work out how many days are left before school starts again?

Priya, a cook, worked all day in a busy kitchen, and her father lived alone on the first floor of an old building. She said to her phone, remind dad to take his pills at eight and call him at nine. The assistant understood two jobs in one sentence. It set a pill reminder for her father at eight and planned a call for nine. Priya also asked it to count how many days of pills were left in the box, and the assistant said six. The pills were expensive, so she did not want to run out by accident. The assistant offered to remind her on Friday to order more, and Priya said yes. She went back to the stove feeling calmer.

Hannah, a gardener, had just met a kind man who sold lemon trees at the market. She said to her phone, add Victor Reyes to my contacts, his number is 555-0142. Then she looked at her note and said, wait, it's 555-0124, I got the last two numbers wrong. The assistant understood that she had fixed a detail and saved the number as 555-0124. Hannah added, put his birthday as the tenth of June, because she wanted to celebrate it with a small plant. The assistant saved that too. It was a long day in the sun, and Hannah smiled as she put her phone away, glad that she would not lose his number.

Ben woke up late with a stale taste in his mouth and a meeting across town. He mumbled to his phone, how long does it take to drive to the office, and send the route to my car screen. The assistant understood two requests in one sentence. First it checked the traffic, using a city website with road works, and said the drive would take thirty-five minutes because of a closed lane. Then it sent the best route to his car screen. Ben jumped up, brushed his teeth, and grabbed his keys. He asked the assistant to message his boss that he would be ten minutes late, and it did. He got in the car and set off.

Mina woke up at three in the morning when the baby monitor crackled. She was too tired to talk much, so she whispered to the speaker, feeding time? The assistant understood that she wanted to know when the baby last ate and said the last bottle was at midnight. Mina rubbed her eyes and said, start timer. The assistant started a timer for twenty minutes so she could skip checking the clock. The baby had gas, so the simple lullaby on the speaker was not helping. Mina said, skip song, and the assistant played the next one, a slower one. Soon the room was quiet again, and Mina went back to bed.

They want a gift idea for a birthday.
Gift ideas?
What should I get my brother for his birthday?
I need a present for my mom, and something that will last.
Any great ideas for a dad who loves fishing?
Find me a gift for under fifty dollars and tell me when the shop closes.
Help, the party is on Saturday and I have nothing for my gram!
What can I give a friend who already has everything?
I would be so thankful if you could suggest something thoughtful and remind me to buy it on Thursday.

Notes help you keep your ideas safe. You can write them down, type them, or say them out loud as a voice note. A funny idea can come at night, and by morning it may fall out of your head, so people say, note this down, or, remember that for me. Each note is an item in a list, and people change them: add a line, take one away, or fix a word. Later they look for old notes by saying, find my note about the garden, or, read me my list from Monday. Short notes are the easiest to find, so many people use simple titles.

Sam, a student, burned his hand on a hot pan while cooking dinner. It hurt, so he said to his phone, my hand is burned, what should I do? The assistant understood that this was first aid and told him to cool the burn under running water for ten minutes. It sounded calm and clear. Sam asked, what's the price of burn cream at the drugstore? The assistant said it was usually a few dollars. Because it was a small burn, he did not need to call anyone. Sam then said, remind me to look at it tomorrow at seven. The assistant set the reminder and said to see a doctor if it looked worse. Sam put a clean cloth on it and kept his personal first aid kit close.

Mrs. Doyle was not good with technology, and a parcel with a new skirt was supposed to come that week. She felt nervous about it, so she spoke to the speaker in the hall. Where is my parcel, and when will it come? she said. The assistant understood two questions in one sentence. It looked up the order and said the parcel was on a truck and would come on Thursday. It also said the maximum wait was two more days. Mrs. Doyle asked it to remind her to check the mailbox in the afternoon, and the assistant said it would. She shut the mailbox, felt proud, and waited for Thursday.

Aiko was new to the city, and the bathroom in her little apartment was always chilly. One morning she saw a crack in the wall and wanted to show her landlord. She said to her phone, take a photo of the bathroom wall. The assistant opened the camera and took the picture. Then she said, create an album called New Apartment and put it in there. The assistant made the album and saved the photo. Aiko also said, remind me tomorrow at seven to send these to the landlord. The assistant set the reminder. Aiko felt better knowing that she had a plan, and she wrapped a warm scarf around her neck.

Omar woke up in the dark. The room was strangely silent, with no hum from the fridge and no light on the clock. Weak light came from the street. His body felt heavy, and his mind was still half asleep, so he said to his phone, it's pitch black in here and the fridge is silent. The assistant understood that he meant the power was out. It turned on the phone flashlight and said to keep the fridge door shut so the food would stay cold. Omar had been trying to stick to a diet, and he laughed that at least the ice cream was safe. He asked the assistant to call the power company, and it did.

Person: remind me to take my pils at noon
Assistant: Which pills should I put in the reminder?
Person: the thick white ones for my blood pressure
Assistant: Got it. Should I remind you every day, or just today?
Person: every day. the board in my shop says lunch is at noon so that works
Assistant: That sounds good. I will remind you every day at noon to take the thick white pills for your blood pressure.

Walter was not good with technology, but he wanted dinner without cooking. He pointed at his speaker and said, order pizza for four people from Tony's, same as last time. The assistant understood that he meant the order he had made before and put it in. It said the pizza would cost twenty-eight dollars and asked if he wanted to add a tip. Walter said, add a good one. The assistant added five dollars. Then Walter said, tell me when it comes. The assistant told him the driver would arrive in about thirty minutes. When the doorbell rang, he opened the door, took the tasty pizza, and thanked the driver. His grandchildren cheered.

name: box_label_maker
does: Makes labels for moving boxes and tells which room each box should go in.
inputs: what is in the box, and the room it belongs to
people say:
- put a label on the box with the light bulbs, kitchen
- write fragile on the glasses box
- the freezer bag stuff is icy cold, mark it to unpack first
- which room does the box with winter coats go to
- make a sticker for each bedroom box

Dana was new to the city and still learning her way around. When she got home, she found a slip on the door about a black parcel. She did not know what to do, so she asked her phone, there's a note about a parcel, I don't want it left outside, I want it held at the post office. The assistant understood that she did not want the parcel left on the step and asked the carrier to hold it at the nearest post office. The parcel held a new phone battery, and Dana could not afford to lose it. The assistant told her which post office had it and when it opened. She wrote down the hours and went to bed relieved.

Kai, a teenager, was lying on the couch and texting the assistant on his phone. Book a haircut for saturday and tell me when the shop closes, he typed. The assistant understood two requests in one sentence. It booked a haircut at eleven on Saturday and said the shop closed at six. Kai was young and had never booked his own haircut before, so he felt a little proud. He was saving money for new shoes, so he asked how much a cut cost. The assistant said it was fifteen dollars. Kai disconnected his earbuds, put his phone on the table, and went to find his wallet.

They want the bedroom light dimmed but not turned off.
Dim the lights, but don't turn them off.
Make it softer in here.
Not so bright, please.
Lower the lamp a bit.
I want to watch a movie, so make the room darker, but not completely dark.
The little girl is excited and can't sleep, so turn the lights down low without switching them off.
Would you mind making the light gentler, as I don't want it off, only quieter?

They want to order the same groceries again.
Reorder.
Order that again.
Same as last time, please.
Buy my usual things.
There is fog outside and I don't want to drive to the store, so can you order my usual stuff?
Arrange delivery for the same things as last week.
Could you please put in my average weekly shop and send it to the house?

They want the heating to turn on at a certain time.
Heating on at seven tomorrow.
Warm the house up before I get up tomorrow at seven.
Have it nice and warm by tomorrow at seven.
Turn on the radiators for tomorrow at seven, please.
I'd like a calm, warm room by tomorrow at seven, since the baby will be playing with her ball on the floor.
Please warn me if the heater can't reach twenty degrees by tomorrow at seven.

Grandma Rosa had baked bread all morning, and the kitchen was very hot. Her grandchildren were coming for lunch. She said to the speaker, excuse me, could you please turn the fan up to a higher level and turn on the air conditioning in the kitchen? I have been baking for hours and my grandchildren are coming, and it is too hot for them. The assistant understood that she wanted the fan on high and the air conditioning started. It told her the kitchen would feel cooler in about ten minutes. Rosa thanked it and sat down by the window. Soon many little feet ran in, and the room was fresh and cool.

Person: I'm just waking up. Give me a workout, but no running.
Assistant: Okay. How many minutes do you have?
Person: Fifteen. I did not sleep well, so I feel a little sad and slow.
Assistant: Then a gentle one with stretching and light squats. Should I start it?
Person: Yes. Just one question: can you count the sets out loud?
Assistant: Yes. I will count each set and tell you when to rest.

Frank, a gardener, came in from the yard feeling sleepy after a long morning of digging. He said to the kitchen speaker, make coffee, two cups. Then he thought again and said, actually just one, my wife is still asleep. The assistant understood that he had changed his mind and told the coffee machine to make one cup. It said the coffee would be ready in three minutes. Frank had a good idea and asked it to play soft music too. As the coffee brewed, the steam seemed to dance above the machine. He poured it, sat at the table, and looked out at his garden with a warm cup in his hands.

Grandpa Lou was eating a banana at the bus stop, and he wanted to go to the market. He asked his phone, when is the next number twelve bus? The assistant understood that he meant the bus on route twelve and said it would come in twenty-five minutes. Lou wanted his daughter to know, so he said, forward the timetable to Emma. The assistant sent it. He also asked about a weekly pass, since he rode the bus often. The assistant said a weekly pass cost eighteen dollars and could be bought on the bus. Lou finished his banana, sat down on the bench, and waited with a smile.

They want to know how far they have walked today.
How far did I walk today?
Steps so far?
Give me my step report.
Have I done ten thousand steps yet?
Tell me out loud how many miles I've gone since the fresh morning air got me out of bed.
Would you please let me know my distance so far, and shout when I pass five miles?

They want to know how much fuel is in the car.
how much gas is left
am i low on fule
Do I have enough fuel to get home?
Check the tank for me.
Will I make it to the next station? The light looks like it's on.
It's a pretty long drive, so please tell me the fuel level, I have only a minute before I leave.
Could you let me know how far I can go on what's in the tank?

Ivy woke up to a drip, drip, drip from the kitchen. Her knee hurt as she walked over the wet floor. Still half asleep, she said to her phone, book a plumber for the kitchen tap at nine. Then she stopped and said, no, the bathroom tap, the kitchen one is fine. The assistant understood that she had fixed a detail and booked the plumber for the bathroom tap at nine. It said the plumber would come from the east side of town. Ivy asked, what do I owe him for a visit like that? The assistant said the visit usually cost sixty dollars. Ivy put a bowl under the drip and made her tea.
